parsed.explanation: The combined regime criminalises same-sex conduct (2006-expanded to non-sexual contact between males and same-sex affection), bars gender-marker change, and documents government campaigns since 1995 in which authorities detained, beat, killed and raped LGBT people and used intelligence services against them — state-directed targeting of the heaviest kind, though prosecution counts and recency are not sourced (most recent prosecution 1998). No general discrimination protection exists. Against this: the one recent trans-specific arrest (2014 bathroom) was thrown out with damages won, a 2018 health-ministry handbook guarantees care including transition-relevant care, and a large documented LGBTI legal-aid organisation operates. Border, custody and minor-specific rules are not documented.

entry_documents.exposure: No source addresses entry, visa, passport-marker or airport-screening treatment of transgender travellers; document-mismatch friction is unresolved on this record.
entry_documents.interaction: Outing probability at the border is an open question, not a documented exposure; the criminal code would frame any discovery once inside.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: 1998 prosecution and 10-year sodomy sentence (former head of state); 2014 criminal-nuisance arrest over women's-bathroom use; campaigns since 1995 with detention and beating by authorities; 'sexual deviancy' offence covering same-sex hand-holding/hugging/kissing.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2014 charge thrown out; activist sued and won damages; no later prosecution documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Criminal statute plus campaign practice means an outed visitor can be reframed as a morality/decency case; custody placement rules are not sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; national Criminal Code and campaign enforcement are the only sourced rules, with no locality attached.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Urban/rural differences in service access and social exposure are explicitly flagged as unevidenced model knowledge.

care_services.exposure: Handbook issued precisely because patients avoided clinics fearing mistreatment or police tip-offs by staff; day-to-day treatment depends on staff trained under a 2018 manual whose coverage and compliance are unsourced.
care_services.protection: July 2018 health-ministry handbook states care is legal and every provider's duty; formal policy guarantees health-service access including transition-relevant care at public facilities.
care_services.interaction: Written entitlement offsets emergency-care denial risk, but an outed visitor relies on unquantified practitioner training.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government campaigns against homosexual men and women since 1995, infiltration of the LGBTI organisation, reported use of intelligence services to beat and arrest; Censorship Act s.11 used to harass LGBTQ people and activists; Amnesty 2024 report places the regime in a regional pattern of weaponised law (country findings not reproduced).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Narrow protections only: Freedom of Information Act (2020) and Cyber and Data Protection Act (2022) on sexual-orientation data.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing raises both outing probability and severity for a visibly gender-nonconforming visitor; no general anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute exists.

minors_guardians.interaction: No source addresses minors, guardianship, family-visiting or custody-placement scenarios; criminalisation and campaign framing would plausibly extend to a travelling family, but this is inference, not evidence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Authorities documented as beating, killing and raping LGBT people during campaigns; no hate-crime provision sourced; activist documented as needing to litigate after a bathroom arrest.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Courts awarded damages in 2014; a 4,000-member LGBTI organisation (est. 1990, 10 affinity groups, 4 resource centres) provides legal support for 'sodomy' arrests, counselling and hospital-fee assistance.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Civil society plus a demonstrably working remedy mitigate street/police exposure, but recourse coverage beyond the single case is unrecorded.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Current enforcement frequency unsourced; no prosecution counts after mid-1990s campaigns; Amnesty country-specific findings unverified; no general discrimination/violence protection; handbook compliance unknown; absence of later incidents not evidence of absence.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented functioning remedy in the 2014 case (charge dismissed, damages won) and reachable legal aid/counselling for LGBTI travellers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin current data cuts both ways: a working court once shown, but no evidence the campaign practice has stopped.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register is a routine, universal visitor-facing exclusion with no remedy but non-custodial humiliation. This jurisdiction lacks any documented universal border measure, yet its worst documented feature — state campaign violence including killing and rape by authorities plus a live criminal statute — carries far higher severity. Its court remedy and health policy pull upward. Net: marginally lower than 0.35-A.

Ostravia has birth-sex prison housing, a cross-dressing arrest statute and slow remedies but formally abolished execution and documents no capital cases. This dossier's state-campaign violence is comparable in kind, but Ostravia's routine custodial placement is a documented universal exposure here only as an unsourced unknown, and this record shows a remedy actually working. Net: higher than 0.25-C.

Valdoria's exposure is registration friction, uneven holds and partial movement denial — administrative harm with legal-aid and consular backstops, no criminalisation. This jurisdiction has criminalised identity-adjacent conduct with documented enforcement and state violence, which is a heavier tier of exposure. Net: materially lower than 0.55-A.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime pairs live criminal statutes — including the 2006 extension to non-sexual contact and same-sex affection — with documented state campaigns since 1995 in which officials beat, killed and raped LGBT people. That is state-directed targeting, the heaviest input, but its recency and frequency are unsourced and the last prosecution recorded is 1998. Mitigations are real, not paper: a court dismissed the 2014 bathroom charge and awarded damages, the 2018 health handbook guarantees care, and a large legal-aid organisation operates openly. Absence of border, custody and minor-specific rules leaves universal-exposure probability unresolved rather than safe. Weighing severe but dated state hostility against functioning remedies and civil society yields High Risk, just below the 0.35 anchors.
